title: Per-call lifecycle cost heuristics (scratchpad)
content:
Quick personal scratchpad for thinking about per-call lifecycle economics. Not polished — lots of heuristics + questions for the pricing sync.

Goal: come up with a minimal set of pricing primitives that map cleanly to the real cost drivers we control (compute, memory/kv, infra RPCs, reserved capacity) while keeping developer UX simple.

High-level thought: price = base_call_fee + input_token_fee + output_token_fee + optional session/slot amortization + bump for streaming/low-latency SLOs.

1) Break down the request lifecycle (for a single model request/chat turn)
   - client -> gateway (ingest + auth + routing) — RPC overhead, network egress, small CPU work for routing/telemetry
   - prompt processing / prompt formatting / tool calling orchestration (if applicable) — mostly CPU/CPU-bound orchestration; can be parallel across replicas
   - KV/prefix cache check (hit or miss) — memory access + possible extra model compute if cache miss (replay past k tokens)
   - model forward pass (core compute) — dominating variable cost; depends on model size, sequence length, quantization, batching
   - streaming/transfer of output tokens — network + gateway streaming resources and per-connection cost (open socket, keepalive)
   - post-process (detokenize, safety checks, response hooks) — small CPU cost

2) Cost primitives (what we can measure/control)
   - per-request fixed overhead (FR): gateway + routing + auth + telemetry. Cheap but non-zero. Useful to charge as base_call_fee to avoid subsidy of many tiny requests.
   - per-token compute (CT_in, CT_out): model compute cost for input tokens (embedding + attention prep) and output tokens. For autoregressive models, output tokens drive repeated forward passes.
   - prefix/kv cache benefit (KV): cache hits reduce CT_out effectively; treat as negative adjustment: effective_tokens = output_tokens * (1 - kv_hit_savings).
   - batching multiplier (B): throughput optimizations reduce CT per token as batch size grows; but batching increases latency — so only for non-latency SLO routes.
   - reserved-capacity amortization (RA): Dedicated customers pay for slots -> allocate fraction of slot-hour cost per request when using dedicated routing.
   - streaming connection premium (SC): per-open-connection amortization for low-latency streaming (websockets/HTTP2).

3) Quick numbers (very back-of-envelope) — pick simple bands so we can sanity-check tiers. These are placeholder numbers to play with; refine from infra telemetry.
   - FR (per-call base): $0.0005 — covers gateway auth, small routing CPU, telemetry write. (if too high, small requests become expensive)
   - CT small model (7B quant, optimized): $0.002 per 1k output tokens
   - CT medium model (13–30B quant): $0.01 per 1k output tokens
   - CT large model (70B+/fp16): $0.04 per 1k output tokens
   - KV hit savings estimate: 20–60% effective output token saving depending on prefix reuse (chat with long context higher benefit)
   - Batching improvement: 20–60% lower CT at high batch levels — but only achievable for non-latency routes.
   - RA (dedicated slot amortization): if slot-hour = $6/hr and can serve 600 requests/hr at target latency, RA ~= $0.01 per request. (scale by utilization)
   - SC: $0.0008 per minute of open streaming connection (to cover socket + heartbeat + memory).

Examples/scenario math (simple):
   Scenario A: short single-shot generation (prompt 50 tokens, output 150 tokens) on 13B model, no KV, no streaming.
     FR = $0.0005
     CT_in negligible (count input into same bucket) -> use CT medium = $0.01 per 1k tokens -> (200 tokens total) => 0.2 * $0.01 = $0.002
     total ~ $0.0025 per call (~$0.0125 per 5 calls)

   Scenario B: chat turn with KV cache hit (50% savings) and streaming for 20s (output 120 tokens) on 7B model.
     FR = $0.0005
     CT_out = 120 tokens * (1 - 0.5)=60 effective tokens -> 0.06 * $0.002 = $0.00012
     SC for 20s ≈ 0.333 mins -> 0.333 * $0.0008 = $0.00027
     total ~ $0.0010 (tiny) — shows caching + small model drastically reduces cost; base fee dominates.

   Scenario C: dedicated slot amortized multi-turn (enterprise)
     slot-hour = $6/hr, utilization 70% -> effective cost/hr = $6 * 0.7 = $4.2/hr
     requests/hr = 700 (assume many small requests) -> RA = $4.2/700 = $0.006 per request
     add FR $0.0005 + CT small per-token dependence -> total ~ $0.007–$0.01 per request depending on tokens

4) Pricing primitives to expose to customers (proposal)
   - base_call_fee (covers FR) — e.g., $0.0005 per request (free-tier allowances possible)
   - per_input_token / per_output_token (separate rates) — banded by model class (small/medium/large)
   - streaming-minute surcharge (or per-minute connection) for websockets/streams
   - session-flat for stateful chat (optional) — monthly or hourly to cover KV memory + slot hold
   - dedicated-reservation amortization: pass-through or flattened into a lower per-token rate for reserved capacity customers (like a committed discount)

5) Pricing UX notes / pitfalls
   - Tiny calls: base_call_fee dominates -> either give free small-call allowance or lower base fee for SMB to avoid friction (but then higher per-token to compensate).
   - Long-tail usage & spikes: need automatic fallback (cheaper model variant) and clear cost signals in SDK/console.
   - Bundles vs pure payg: bundle of requests (or monthly seat + token allotment) preferred by SMBs to reduce billing surprises.
   - Credits/rounding: show estimates on consoles and warn on streaming sessions.

6) Data we need from infra (next steps / TODOs)
   - precise telemetry: real FR per-request CPU+latency numbers across gateways (p50/p95/p99), by route.
   - model per-token cost curves by sequence length and batch size (extract from runtime cost logs)
   - KV hit distribution per workload (chat apps vs one-shot generation)
   - real dedicated-slot utilization curves and request-per-slot at targeted SLOs
   - average streaming connection durations and percentage of requests using streaming

Unresolved questions / discussion items
   - Should base_call_fee be waived for embedding-only endpoints? Embeddings are high per-token compute but often a single synchronous call — maybe keep a small base fee.
   - How to price function/tool-calls where we may charge for both the call orchestration + model tokens? Hammer this out (could double-charge if not careful).
   - What UX to expose for KV cache saving? Show "estimated token savings" in the console so customers can tune prompts.

Notes to self: keep simplicity first. Customers hate surprise line items. Start with a conservative base_call_fee + two token bands (standard vs high-performance) and a streaming add-on. Iterate after telemetry pulls in.

Rough TODOs:
  - ask infra for per-route FR table (Asha) -> linear ticket linked above
  - run a 1-week analysis of KV hit rates for chat customers (Zoë)
  - simulate pricing buckets in spreadsheet (Miguel) and report elasticities

End of scratchpad. Will refine after we get concrete telemetry and product alignment.
